refreshed_by: the agent library cycle (every 6 hours); edit this file, then rebuild the academy

structure.repository: one repository for the whole site, 140+ branches

branches.main: the shell: shared header, menu and runtime, landing page, build tools, themes.json, sections.lock, shared rules, CI. Site-wide changes only, by pull request labelled site-wide.
branches.theme branches: one webapp per branch (for example kissed-frogs, nomenclature, projects, maps, cedwyn-movie); the branch folder (usually public/) is copied to /{id}/ at build time
branches.section/{id}: snapshot branches for crawled sections (research, wiki, fcg, app, chat, estate, patagonia, cyberspace), pinned by sections.lock and moved by the sections-ci workflow
branches.agents: this academy (public/ copied to /academy/ outside the theme list, noindex)
branches.hive: hive state (roster, board, join file, batons) served at /hive/
branches.site: the assembled output the static host serves

structure.registry: themes.json on main lists every webapp (id, titles in English, Welsh and Spanish, branch, folder, group); data/site-areas.json groups 44 source themes into 36 visitor areas. Welsh mirrors live under /wales/{section}/ and Spanish under /argentina/{section}/.
build_pipeline: assemble: copy each branch folder, run an optional per-theme build, read a pinned section snapshot, or crawl a running app
site: root page and shared runtime
self-contain: add the shared three-row header from /_cedwyn/ghf/
privacy scrub (fails the build on working-process attribution)
views: derive each migrated webapp's view and render its pages (never fails the build; the app falls back to its static pages)
outbound-link guard, self-contained test, link audit, public-voice check
publish to branch site; the static host serves it
build_facts: a full build takes about 30–50 minutes
builds queue and each one finishes (cancel-in-progress is off on main); never cancel or re-dispatch a build
a push to a theme branch does not start a build; the next build carries it
a section snapshot moves only through sections-ci
builds regenerate everything: fix sources, never the built output
each webapp's header graph plots only that webapp's own view database (<app>/_db/view.json), never the central catalogue; a build check fails any graph whose points do not trace to its own app's view
files served only through the service worker (view.json, _ui templates, programme data) must be on the build's keep-list, or a plain fetch answers 404
structure.shared_header: one JSON file per site under web/_cedwyn/ghf/sites/, plus themes.json and site-areas.json, produce the uniform header and menu that titles every page; pages therefore never repeat a big title
structure.versions: /_cedwyn/versions.json is the one site-wide version scheme: the newest edition of any product is v0.0.2, the one before it v0.0.1, older ones -v0.0.2, -v0.0.3 and so on (no -v0.0.1); read by /documentary/ and /ebooks/
structure.discovery: /llms.txt, /agents.json, robots.txt and one alternate link plus ai-agents meta per page head point machines at /academy/; nothing machine-facing appears on human pages

data.master: data/core/ in git (JSON Schema 2020-12): one record per thing

record_fields.title: neutral headline
record_fields.transcript: verbatim text where held, with its status
record_fields.interpretation: our reading, marked as interpretation; ranked competing readings allowed
record_fields.provenance: source only: holder, reference, date, how obtained (never who found it)
record_fields.scope: disposition (in_scope, not_this_property, separate_property, out_of_scope, name_correction, dating_correction, assertion_only, context_only, on_hold), reason, distinct_from, tags
record_fields.places / people / links: ids and typed links (cites, distinct_from, same_as_candidate, supersedes, answers)
record_fields.public: false rows never leave the build

compile_chain: the catalogue SQLite built at site build (core records and links; served in chunks over HTTP range requests at /db/, no server calls)
the D1 edge database mirrored from core, read through the catalogue read API (/api/catalogue); a mirror, never the source
data.view_dbs: each webapp gets its own small database at /{app}/_db/view.json, derived from core by a written selection rule in data/views/{app}.view.json (select by kind and fields, project public fields only, include links). Nobody edits a view by hand. Note: the build serves data files from the catalogue, so a plain fetch of a view file may answer 404 while the page itself is rendered at build time.
data.pilot: Kissed Frogs: view = core records whose scope disposition marks them as looked-like-the-farm-but-not; its index and 49 detail pages render from the view (live 30 Oct 2026). Llandough Farm (a separate farm, NLW D 219/9–13) is its canonical card.
data.near_a2ui: each page is a component list in the A2UI v0.9 shape (createSurface, a flat updateComponents list, updateDataModel bound by JSON pointer) rendered by one shared renderer at build time, with an optional small client renderer; components come only from the Cedwyn catalog, which maps one-to-one to the CSS classes the site already uses, so the design stays the same. Unknown component = build error. Agents can propose a page as a component list without injecting HTML or script.
data.rollback: per webapp: set "enabled": false in its view file (one-line commit); the next build serves the branch's static pages again. Core: revert the data/core commit. Nothing force-pushes or deletes history.
gates: no public:false rows or private fields; privacy scrub zero
public voice: banned words zero, neutral third person

metrics.HCR: hard-coded records left on an app's pages (target 0)
metrics.COV: share of the app's pages generated from its view (target 100%)
metrics.PAR: pixel difference against the baseline at 390 px and 1280 px (at most 2% per page type, no layout shift)
metrics.SIZE: view at most 1 MB; page weight at most baseline + 5%

autoresearch_pattern.shape: hypothesis -> smallest change -> measure -> keep or discard
rules: a fixed program file, one editable surface, a fixed time budget and one fixed metric
keep a change only if the metric improves; otherwise revert
log every experiment, kept or discarded
never change the metric to make a result look good

migration_flywheel.name: Claim and baseline
migration_flywheel.what: Claim the webapp on the project board (no two agents on one app). Screenshot every page type at 390 px and 1280 px, light and dark; save the visible text and the list of record ids shown.

migration_flywheel.name: Hypothesis
migration_flywheel.what: One sentence: the [record type] on {page} can be expressed as view rule R plus template T with no visual change.

migration_flywheel.name: Smallest change
migration_flywheel.what: In order, only what the hypothesis needs: add missing records to data/core; write the view rule in data/views/{app}.view.json; write the page template as a component list (_ui/{page}.a2ui.json) using catalog components only.

migration_flywheel.name: Measure
migration_flywheel.what: Render locally; run the schema validator, the privacy test, the parity harness and the metrics (hard-coded records, coverage, parity).

migration_flywheel.name: Keep or discard
migration_flywheel.what: Keep only if every gate passes and hard-coded records fell or coverage rose with parity in bounds; otherwise revert. Log one results row either way.

migration_flywheel.name: Ship, verify, record
migration_flywheel.what: Small commits, fast-forward only; let a running build finish; verify live with a cache-busted fetch at 390 px and desktop; record the metrics and commit on the task. Three discarded hypotheses in a row on one app go to the problems queue.

loops.name: Daily site flywheel
loops.does: Measures every farm site (status, phone-width render, score), then works each site's own program file in priority order: safe automatic fixes only, everything else logged as a proposal.
inputs: the site list and one program file per site
outputs: proposals for anything not safe to automate
a scored log row per check
touches: every Cedwyn section (check), branches it is allowed to fix
guardrails: sites owned by another running worker are check-and-report only
fixes verified live at 390 px before they count
the legacy wiki is never edited beyond redirects
no force-push; commits carry the house sign-off

loops.name: Email ingest
loops.does: Reads new project mail (read-only), classifies it, reads attachments, and feeds the record: the disclosure manifest, the roadmap and dartboard, candidate catalogue entries and missing-record candidates, and the matching case task on the project board.
inputs: new project mail since the last run
attachments (locked ones recorded as locked, never opened by force)
outputs: catalogue and missing-record candidates for the research cycles
a dated paragraph on the matching case task
a site build when none is queued
guardrails: mail is read, never sent or drafted
personal-data material is read but held privately
scope filter: Great House Farm / cedwyn mail only

loops.name: Correspondence flywheel
loops.does: Works out who needs a reply, a chaser, an escalation, a forward or a first contact, and writes one hive draft task per item on the project board; between items it does housekeeping on existing tasks.
outputs: triage notes on unsent tasks when a new fact exists
guardrails: drafts only: never sent, never marked sent by an agent
research and disclosure mail only, never marketing
status values only not-started or completed

loops.name: Hive drafts and review gates
loops.does: The multi-agent review room at /hive/ (the old hive host forwards there). Each seat takes its turns on draft letters: one material review per turn, a semantic version bump and a signed changelog line, then passes the turn on. A draft becomes ready only at the exact-version gate: ten reviews from at least four different seats on the same frozen version.
inputs: draft tasks whose turn is this seat's
outputs: versioned reviews with signed changelog entries
a mail draft for human review only after every gate passes
guardrails: never delete another agent's lines
re-check the last-modified time before writing
turns idle past the skip window allow only the permitted route action
a person reviews and sends; agents never send

loops.name: Hive board sync
loops.does: Rebuilds the hive board (review counts, seats, percentage to ready, synced time) from the project board, read-only, and commits it only if something changed.
inputs: task subjects, last-modified times and changelog counts (no bodies)
outputs: the hive board JSON with a synced_at stamp
guardrails: read-only on the project board
never drops another agent's row
JSON validated before commit
commits only when changed

loops.name: Repository and project-board sync
loops.does: Studies new commits, pull requests and issues and the live work board, notes them on matching tasks, closes tasks only when verified live, and opens tasks for outstanding work.
inputs: repository activity since the last run
touches: the project board (the site is read-only here)
guardrails: repository read-only
duplicate check before any new task
hive turn, sales and personal tasks are never touched

loops.name: Online gap finder
loops.does: Searches public archives, catalogues, newspapers, registers and books for material about the farm that is not yet on Cedwyn, and turns each genuine gap into a task naming the area it belongs in.
inputs: the live site (sitemap, research, evidence catalogue)
outputs: 3–8 gap tasks per run, each with source, summary and target page
touches: the project board; agents then add the material to /research/, /wiki/, /wales/ and other areas
guardrails: never edits the site itself
duplicate and seen checks first
nothing about family holdings or addresses

loops.name: Book search
loops.cadence: search every 59 minutes; findings table every 3 hours
loops.does: Searches published books for passages overlapping what the site carries about the farm, its families and places, under every name variant, and records each passage with its exact sentence and citation.
inputs: a keyword ledger that retires the most productive keywords each cycle
outputs: rows in the research findings table (book, exact sentence, citation)
touches: /research/ (section branch research, live after the sections workflow moves the pin)
guardrails: exact quotation with the reference; inference labelled as inference
the two Llandoughs and same-name farms checked before a passage is used
significant passages checked on the page itself before anyone is told
rows reach the main register only by pull request, with the whole file passing the repository's agent lint

loops.name: First-seen detector
loops.does: Compares a baseline of known farm records online against the latest crawl; a record that quietly appears is verified against its live page and dated captures and published on the first-seen register.
outputs: verified first-seen entries with the dated evidence of absence
guardrails: an entry is published only after verification
neutral dated wording: quiet release or announced disclosure, no verdict

loops.name: Farm page recapture (Watchtower)
loops.does: Recaptures outside pages about the farm's history and heritage and records before and after copies, so any change made by an outside site is caught.
inputs: the list of watched outside pages
guardrails: no alerts for layout changes; only substantive history content counts
robots rules honoured; blocked hosts noted, not forced
skipped when the disk is low

loops.name: Intel flywheel
loops.does: Reviews everything known, plots it many ways (periodicity, sequences, who answered and who stayed silent), and publishes blank evidence pages with catalogue ids for records that should exist by statute, practice or cross-reference but are not held.
inputs: the latest research and reopen-loop reports
outputs: charts and findings re-ranked with what cuts against them
guardrails: commits only to section/research
interpretation is labelled as interpretation
what cuts against a finding is shown beside it

loops.name: Reopen loop
loops.does: Small one-hypothesis experiments against a fixed metric (the three limbs of the legal test for reopening a judgment) to rank grounds for reopening the 1987 judgment.
outputs: the programme highlight report section on prospective triggers (only when the top three change)
the Mr Wolf leaderboard row for a ground whose limb score changed
guardrails: the metric is fixed; never changed to make a result look better
labelled as prospective, never a finding of any court
read-only research

loops.name: Great House Farm research cycle
loops.does: Starts with a change-check of the live sections, then follows the most promising untried route to evidence and artefacts not yet in Cedwyn.
inputs: the last cycle report and next-cycle brief
outputs: new findings in the findings log
touches: feeds /research/ through the intel flywheel and email ingest
guardrails: read-only: never edits the family sites, orders documents or files requests
strict alert bar; the primary source is re-read before any alert

loops.name: Problems flywheel
loops.does: Every blocker or problem goes into one queue instead of to a person. Each open problem gets autoresearch cycles (hypothesis, smallest real test, result logged, keep or discard) until solved; only after six hours of looping with no route left is it marked unsolvable.
inputs: the problems queue (up to three open problems per run, oldest first)
outputs: hypothesis / action / result lines per problem
solved or unsolvable status with evidence
touches: any area, within that area's owner and commit rules
guardrails: decisions are made from standing rules and evidence, with the reasoning recorded
never cancels or dispatches a site build while others run
no commits to a branch another worker owns that day; a proposed patch instead

loops.name: Skills harvest
loops.does: Finds new practitioner playbooks for online sales and marketing (deliverability, testing, search and AI visibility, social growth, launches) and writes each as a short how-to with sources and how it applies to Cedwyn.
guardrails: free tools only, small installs only, none when disk is low
sources named as plain text

loops.name: Sales fix
loops.does: Checks e-book sales; with none, diagnoses why along the funnel (traffic, reach, sign-ups, the buy path walked at phone width) and does the one highest-leverage fix it can make that day, verified live.
inputs: its own log of past fixes
outputs: a log row with numbers and how the fix is measured next run
touches: /ebooks/, /shop/, link targets, channel bios and video descriptions
guardrails: prices are never changed by an agent
no paid ads, bought followers or messages to strangers
a fix that already failed is not repeated

loops.name: Business development
loops.cadence: plan daily 09:00 UK; execute every 2 hours 10:00–22:00
loops.does: Writes the next 24 hours' weighted plan on the project board before any work, then executes the tasks in weight order with care, recording outcomes and lessons in the growth project.
guardrails: plan before work
zero spend; no bought reach
price changes, new channels and press are proposals

loops.name: Daily auto-social
loops.does: Wakes the blog's daily post and posts at most one new item per channel, only once the page and image are live, each linking back to Cedwyn.
inputs: the newest blog post and its image
outputs: at most one post per channel per day, never a duplicate
guardrails: at least four hours between posts per channel
a post held by the safety scan is not forced
no posting to communities, no direct messages

loops.name: Short videos to YouTube Shorts
loops.cadence: with each new short story clip; uploads within the daily quota, queued past it
loops.does: Every short story clip made for the series goes to YouTube Shorts as well as the photo channel: one important moment of the story per clip, a search-friendly title, a thumbnail from the gallery images, and a description that opens with the site link and names its sources (news footage, e-book, photographs, catalogued evidence).
inputs: the series plan of next story beats in date order
outputs: Shorts with titles, thumbnails and descriptions
a queue for anything past the daily quota
guardrails: never a duplicate upload
no version hashtags
strict chronology; each clip tied to a catalogued evidence page or e-book chapter

loops.name: Documentary scenes
loops.does: Takes the next item in the re-render queue or the next unfilled frame of the chronology and produces one short scene: one dated moment, who was there, what was most likely said, with Welsh spoken where the period calls for it and subtitles.
inputs: the scene and shot packages in the public film-studio repository
outputs: the next door opened on the documentary page
the script kept ten frames ahead
guardrails: strict date order; no narrator and no fourth wall from scene 3
reconstruction only; no likeness of real family members
a blocking pre-publish quality gate: 24 fps end to end, cut from original renders, two-pass encode, -16 LUFS, frames of every talking shot looked at
spend only within the film's own daily budget; waits and skips are logged as problems
one unit at a time: take the next unit not done, do that step, store, update the manifest, commit, then pick again; media are repository release files with content ids
the chronology gate flags any gap over about 150 years; in-between scenes show only records of the estate's own ground, else a documented-silence card
twelve files per scene: three native-language performances times four subtitle states, subtitles burned in at build

loops.name: Agent library cycle
loops.does: Reads what agents learned since the last cycle, distils only durable public-safe facts into the academy, regenerates the work board from real gaps, refreshes this architecture section, rebuilds, scans (0 hits required), publishes to the agents branch and checks it live.
inputs: memory notes, lessons, runners, skills and worker reports
the architecture plan, the flywheel list and the webapp registry
guardrails: machine-facing only: nothing on human pages
publishes only to the agents branch, never main
scanner must report zero hits

loops.name: Programme office review
loops.does: Refreshes the inputs for each major objective, advances the cheapest next action that needs no sign-off, scores and rates each objective, and republishes the programme pages.
inputs: worker reports since the last review
guardrails: commits only to the projects branch
prices, publishing, new channels, press and spend are proposals
companies only for outreach drafts

loops.name: Growth report
loops.does: Measures the week: visitors, followers per channel, sign-ups and sales, search coverage; answers public questions; picks next week's one priority.
outputs: three lines on traffic, sign-ups and sales, and next week's priority
touches: measurement only; public replies on the project's own posts
guardrails: read-only on analytics
drafts only for email replies

loops.name: Visibility check
loops.does: Ranks the site for a fixed query set, asks a fixed set of questions of an AI assistant and counts mentions of the site, checks that AI crawlers reach it and notes three peer heritage sites.
inputs: the fixed query and question sets
outputs: scores and up to five tagged actions
touches: measurement only; actions go to on-page or promotion queues
guardrails: read-only
the query set is fixed so weeks compare

loops.name: On-page flywheel
loops.does: Audits every section for page titles and descriptions, share cards, sitemap, robots and llms files, structured data, the buy path and the sign-up strip; fixes markup only.
outputs: markup fixes, an audit score, proposals for body text or design
guardrails: body text and design changes are proposals
verified live at 390 px
commits only when no other worker is committing to that branch

loops.name: Quote pack
loops.does: Makes three quote cards from verbatim period-record lines with their source lines, plus a cover, posts them as one carousel and adds them to the quotes page linking each to its evidence page.
guardrails: verbatim quotes with their source lines only
no accusations about named people

loops.name: Academy member sync
loops.does: Keeps the membership list of the human learning area at /learn/ in step with the checkout records.
guardrails: read-only on the checkout side
stops once the site can read the checkout records itself

loops.name: Contacts flywheel
loops.does: Finds institutions and groups not yet contacted that are likely to hold information, records or artefacts, works out what each may hold, and writes a draft for the hive.
inputs: who has been contacted (sent mail, the project board, the drafts engine)
outputs: 3–6 new candidates with what each may hold
guardrails: institutions only; never private individuals
drafts only

loops.name: Nightly drafts engine
loops.does: Keeps every due information-request draft and chaser written, in the thread it belongs to, ready for review; a chaser only the day after a deadline lapses and only when no reply has arrived.
inputs: new mail since the last run
outputs: draft tasks in the hive format
guardrails: never a chaser before a deadline
never sends; never duplicates an open draft

loops.name: Webapp migration flywheel
loops.cadence: one webapp at a time, per the programme plan
loops.does: Moves one webapp at a time to pages generated from its own view of the central catalogue, keeping the existing design. Six steps per webapp (below).
inputs: the webapp's current pages and baseline screenshots
outputs: parity screenshots at 390 px and desktop
touches: one webapp per loop; main only for data/core, data/views, tools and workflow
guardrails: claim the webapp first; never work one another agent holds
discard any change that breaks a gate
strangler fig: static pages stay until parity is proven; one-line rollback

loops.name: Version standard
loops.does: Audits every webapp and the live site against the version ladder and version picker rule (standing order 47) and fixes small drift: wording, a missing (i) changelog icon, a wrongly computed step price, a missing changelog row.
inputs: the version standard document on main
outputs: small fixes on the owning branch
guardrails: never invents a price; prices come from the store's data
never touches checkout code
owner-edited files get a patch, not an overwrite
never starts or cancels a site build while one runs

loops.name: Releases
loops.cadence: after every change that goes live
loops.does: Cuts a tagged release with a new semantic version for every branch or webapp change, at the commit that is actually live (standing order 44).
inputs: the site build's served stamp and section pins
outputs: an annotated tag named <branch>-vX.Y.Z and a release with neutral notes
guardrails: never tags queued or unbuilt work; it is listed as the next release
a pending hosting preview record is not a deploy; check the build run, the production deploys and the served stamp
release notes are public: same wording rules as the site
